newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN FALLS AS PESSIMISM RETURNS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN FALLS AS PESSIMISM RETURNS.

text.p: The Czech crown lost more than 50 basis points against the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket in early trading on Friday with dealers blaming a renewed bout of pessismism about the currency's medium term prospects.
At 0705 GMT the crown was trading at 30.640 to the dollar and 17.959 to the mark implying a deviation from the basket mid-point of minus 2.67 percent from around minus 2.1 percent at the open.

Breta Tichanek of ING Barings said the fall of the crown may have been driven by scepticism about central bank remarks earlier in the week that it would intervene and even raise interest rates to protect the crown if the need arose.

In response to the comments, the crown immediately strengthened by more than half a percentage point against the basket but dealers said the central bank's purely verbal interventions may be becoming too frequent to have a lasting affect.
"We are agian only at the level of formal announcements that are not changing any fundamentals at all," said Tichanek.
Tichanek doubted the central bank actually would raise interest rates to protect the crown while the Czech economy continued to slow down.
